newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo stocks rise after Japan trade data.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo stocks rise after Japan trade data.

text.p: Tokyo stocks rose moderately early on Wednesday after the release of data showing a surge in Japan's current account surplus in May had only a limited impact on currency rates, brokers said.
They said strength in U.S. markets overnight also buoyed stock prices.
Brokers said blue-chip issues which had been falling in a corrective movement in recent sessions were continuing to attract interest.
After 21 minutes of trade, the Nikkei average was up 75.00 points or 0.38 percent at 19,928.89. September Nikkei futures were unchanged at 19,920.

The Finance Ministry announced on Wednesday that contentious surplus in Japan's current account -- the broadest measure of trade in goods and services -- jumped 154.9 percent to 906.8 billion yen in May, rising for second month in a row.
The surplus in merchandise trade, often a source of bitter rows with United States, surged 118.6 percent to 927.9 billion yen in May from a year earlier, it said.
At Wednesday's rate of around 113 yen to the dollar, the overall current account surplus totalled $8.02 billion, while the trade surplus stood at $8.21 billion.
